differential: Idiopathic Generalized Epilepsy
Recurrent seizures in this age group are a classic presentation for primary epilepsy syndromes, which are often genetic in origin.
Focal Epilepsy
A localized brain abnormality, such as cortical dysplasia or a scar, can act as an irritative focus and cause recurrent seizures.
Brain Tumor
A space-occupying lesion can irritate the surrounding cerebral cortex, provoking recurrent seizure activity.
CNS Infection (Encephalitis)
Inflammation of the brain parenchyma from an infectious agent can cause neuronal hyperexcitability and recurrent seizures.
Autoimmune Encephalitis
Antibody-mediated inflammation of the central nervous system is an important and treatable cause of new-onset seizures in children.
